dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Hi, yeah, hello. Um, I know it's Sunday and City Hall's closed, so I wasn't sure if anybody would even pick up. I saw this number was the storm line, so, hmm, I figured I'd try it.
You got the right place. The storm line stays staffed on weekends. What's going on?

Okay. So it's about snow. Well, not a lot of snow, it's just a dusting, really. But it's freezing out, like wicked cold, been that way all week, so everything that's down is just ice. Let me see, where do I start.
Take your time. Where are you calling about?
It's my mother's house, forty-one Wellington Avenue. Fifth Ward. I'm calling for her, she doesn't really do the phone. I'm her daughter, Carmela.
Okay, Carmela, forty-one Wellington Avenue. And what's the problem there?

It's the sidewalk down by the school. Not in front of her house, it's, um, the stretch near the school that she walks along. Nobody ever cleared it. Not after the last couple of snowfalls, and now it's all packed down and icy under this dusting. I walked it this morning and I about went down.
Alright, so the sidewalk near the school on Wellington hasn't been cleared. Is that the school side of the street, or across from it?
Hmm. School side. No wait, let me think. Her house is on the left going toward the school, and the school's on the right. So, across from her. The sidewalk along the school itself. That one.
Got it, the sidewalk along the school, on the opposite side from her house. I'll note that down. Is it the whole length or just parts?

Pretty much the whole length. Maybe, um, there's one little bit by the corner that somebody shoveled, but the rest, nothing. It's honestly annoying, because the street itself is fine, the plow came through, but the sidewalk where the kids walk is a skating rink.
Understood. I'll pass it along as an uncleared sidewalk by the school. Anything else with it?

Yeah, can somebody bring sand? Or salt, whatever you've got. Even just sand. My mother's got to get down that way for her appointments and I don't love it. Actually, I could probably grab a bucket myself if you do, like, a pickup spot? But I don't know if you do that.

Let me see what I can tell you. I'll put in the request for sand on that stretch. As for a bucket for her own walk, I'd want to check with the crew supervisor on whether there's a place to pick some up. Can I get a number in case someone calls you back?
Sure. It's four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-eight-one.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-eight-one. That's you, Carmela?
That's me, yep.
Good. So that's the sidewalk along the school on Wellington, across from number forty-one, not cleared, icy, and you'd like sand put down, plus a question about picking some up yourself.

Right, that's it. Um, and honestly, don't think I'm rushing you. I've got the whole afternoon free, and it's so quiet out today, with everybody inside because of the cold. I kind of like it. So I'm in no hurry.

Well, that's a nice way to spend a Sunday. I'll tell you, the school sidewalks can fall between the cracks sometimes depending on who's responsible, so I'll flag it so it gets looked at Monday morning at the latest.
Monday. Okay. Hmm, I mean, it's still going to be icy tonight, but fine. Can't somebody put sand down today?
I'll mark it as a safety request, so the on-call crew can see it. I can't tell you they'll get there tonight, but it won't sit until the work week if they've got someone free.
Okay. That's fair, I guess. Just, it's every time. The street gets done and the sidewalk by the school doesn't.
I hear you. I've got it written down with your mother's address as the reference point. If the supervisor has a pickup spot for sand, they'll mention it when they call.
Alright. Thanks, Lorraine. Appreciate you picking up on a Sunday.
Anytime. Stay warm, and tell your mother to watch her step.
Will do. Bye.
